body:
## Summary

- keep Triton-swizzled MXFP4 expert weights and scales registered on the layer
- serialize non-contiguous postprocessed tensors through contiguous CPU snapshots
- keep wrapper-backed runtime tensors out of CPU/offload-group parameter remapping
- add CPU regressions for a fresh-layer sharded round trip and the offloader guard

## Root cause

The Triton MXFP4 post-load path moved the swizzled `w13` and `w2` weight wrappers onto the quantization method and deleted the registered layer parameters. `ShardedStateLoader.save_model` only exports `model.state_dict()`, so those runtime weights were omitted.

On reload, SGLang postprocesses freshly initialized placeholders before it builds the expected state dict. The missing weights therefore disappeared from both the checkpoint and the expected-key set, and loading silently succeeded with placeholder runtime weights. The swizzled scales held by `PrecisionConfig` had the same stale-storage problem even though the original scale parameters remained registered.

This change rebinds all four Triton runtime tensors (two weights and two scales) to their existing registered `Parameter` objects. The module state and kernel wrappers then share the same backing storage, so sharded-load copies update the tensors actually consumed by the kernels. Parameter identity and weight-loader attributes are preserved.

The Hopper swizzle can produce non-contiguous runtime tensors. Safetensors rejects those tensors, so the exporter materializes contiguous CPU snapshots at the save boundary without changing the live runtime layout.

## CPU offload compatibility

Triton wrappers live outside the module parameter mapping temporarily installed by `functional_call`. The four wrapper-backed Parameters are therefore marked to remain on device, and both offloader implementations honor that marker. This preserves the previous effective behavior of the hidden Triton tensors while allowing them to remain registered for serialization.

Fixes #34448

## Validation

- focused CPU regression with import-only stubs for unavailable GPU dependencies: `2 tests`, `OK`
  - creates source and zero-initialized destination layers through the real MXFP4 `create_weights`
  - runs the real MXFP4 post-load method with only the Triton layout conversion mocked
  - saves through the real `ShardedStateLoader`, reloads every safetensors entry into the fresh destination state, and verifies both weights and scales consumed by the runtime wrappers
  - verifies wrapper-backed Parameters are excluded from CPU offload
- the same sharded round-trip regression against current `upstream/main@b3bffef70a` fails as expected because `w13_weight` is absent after postprocessing
- `python3 scripts/ci/check_registered_tests.py`
- Black (`--check`) on all four changed files
- isort (`--check-only`) on the new test
- Ruff (`F401`, `F821`, `UP037`) on all four changed files
- `git diff --check`
- `python3 -m py_compile test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_mxfp4_sharded_state.py`

The CPU tests are registered in `base-a-test-cpu`.

- reporter validation on the original GH200, TP=2 reproduction: the sharded export increased from the broken `4.0G` result to `14G`, resolving the reported missing-weight export symptom ([result](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34558#issuecomment-5293077326))

A full save-reload logits comparison has not yet been reported. Project CI is still pending.
